Datasets: the data a view reads

Every dataset a view or widget can read — SATOM's nine built-in queries, one dataset per device-object type for every product (hundreds), and the ones administrators publish — with their keys, columns, masking, scoping, relations and limits.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.plugin_studio
📍 WhereReport Studio editor → Datasets (read-only); Python console → Data bundle; SATOM Builder → Datasets tab and Library
On this page
  • In one paragraph
  • The three sources
  • Built-in datasets

In one paragraph#

A view never queries anything. It declares dataset keys and SATOM hands it each one as {{ <key>.rows }} — a list of rows, each a dict of column → value — and {{ <key>.columns }}. Datasets come from three sources: SATOM's nine built-in queries, one per device-object type the device cache holds (every product: FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator), and the administrator datasets someone built and published in Administrator → Database. They are listed together, grouped and searchable, in every picker.

The three sources#

Source Keys Built by Group in the picker
Built-in 9 fixed keys (below) SATOM's code Built-in
Device objects <product>_<type> Generated from the device cache, nothing to write FortiWeb objects, FortiWeb objects (deep layer), FortiGate objects, …
Administrator admin_<name> An administrator, with the no-SQL query builder (how) Administrator datasets

Every key is a valid Jinja name: {{ fortiweb_vip.rows }}, {{ admin_policy_inventory.rows }}. {{ data["<key>"] }} works too.

Built-in datasets#

Key Rows Columns
fleet_appliances Every managed device id, name, kind, firmware, host, port
server_policies Cached FortiWeb server policies appliance_id, name, deployment_mode, vserver, server_pool, status
server_policies_full Cached server policies, rich appliance_id, device, policy, deployment_mode, vserver, server_pool, wpp, status, traffic_log, monitor_mode, https_service, service, comment, appid (the App ID parsed from the comment)
server_pools Cached server pools appliance_id, name, type, protocol
web_protection_profiles Cached WAF profiles appliance_id, name, kind (inline / offline), signature_rule, bot_policy (always empty: the cache does not keep it)
certificates Certificate Manager certificates (no key material) id, common_name (the certificate's name), appliance_id, status, not_after (expiry)
audit_recent The 200 most recent audit-log rows timestamp, username, action, target, product
fleet_counts One row of totals devices, server_policies, certificates
scheduled_actions Scheduled actions name, action_key, schedule_kind, enabled, next_run, product

Values of the built-in datasets arrive as text ("7", "True"), an empty value as "".

ℹ️Note

Fixed in 4.3.0: server_policies, web_protection_profiles, certificates and scheduled_actions were always empty (their queries named columns their tables do not have), and policies, pools and WAF profiles showed twice (their cache tables keep one row per cache layer). They now return one row per object.

Device-object datasets#

SATOM keeps a copy of every device's configuration in its cache — every object and sub-object, per product. Each object type in that cache is a dataset:

Part of the key Meaning Example
<product> fortiweb, fortigate, fortiadc, fortianalyzer, fortiauthenticator fortigate_…
deep_ (only for the deep layer) FortiWeb's deep capture: the full nested tree of policies and profiles fortiweb_deep_server_policy
<type> The cache's name of the object type, lower case, - read as _ firewall_policy, vip, server_pool
__<sub> A sub-object (a table inside an object) fortiadc_load_balance_pool__pool_member

Columns, always in this order:

Column Meaning
id The row's id in SATOM's cache (stable while the object is unchanged)
appliance_id The device it was read from (a number)
device That device's name
mkey The object's name or id on the device — what other objects refer to
parent_id For a sub-object, the id of its parent row; empty otherwise
the object's fields As the cache holds them, - read as _ (deployment-mode → deployment_mode); at most 120 — the fields people look for first (name, status, action, interface, addresses, ports, pool…), then the ones that hold a value; the device API's bookkeeping fields q_… and _… are left out; a field named id becomes f_id

Masking. A field whose name says secret — containing passw, passwd, psk, secret, token, private, or ending in key — reads ******** (empty stays empty). The picker and the Library mark masked columns.

Which exist on your server. A type is listed only once a device of that product has been synced: the list follows your fleet. On a typical lab fleet there are about 600 (FortiWeb ~340 including the deep layer, FortiADC ~145, FortiGate ~50, FortiAnalyzer ~50, FortiAuthenticator ~15). New types appear within five minutes of a sync.

Rows: at most 1,000 per dataset, ordered by device and position.

🧪Example — Find what you need

Search the picker for the thing you want: vip, firewall_policy, certificate, pool_member, interface. Each entry shows its key and its number of columns; the Library of SATOM Builder (and the Datasets tab of a Builder project) shows every column, which ones are masked and how the dataset relates to others.

Administrator datasets#

When no dataset gives what a view needs — a join of two tables, a filter, a total per device — an administrator builds one with the same no-SQL query builder as the database reports and publishes it. Its key is admin_<name>, its columns are the ones its query selects (a column keeps its own name, or <table>_<column> when two tables have a column with that name; aggregates read n, sum_<col>, count_distinct_<col>…). → Build a plugin dataset.

Since 4.4.0 an administrator can also Generate joined datasets: one click writes, one ADOM each, the joins the device cache allows — every list with its parent (admin_fortigate_firewall_policy__srcaddr_with_parent), every field that names another object resolved, and the chains a fleet asks (admin_fortigate_address_in_rules_as_source: each address with the rules that use it). Look for those before asking for a new one; Browse the N datasets in the same tab lists them all.

Who sees which rows#

Every dataset is evaluated for the person who opens the view, at that moment:

  • only the devices of their ADOM, and maintenance devices only if their profile may see them;
  • audit_recent only with audit.view;
  • an administrator dataset's query gets the viewer's ADOM added to every table it reads, by SATOM, every time.

In a product's ADOM the picker offers that product's device-object datasets only (FortiWeb objects in the FortiWeb ADOM…), plus the built-in ones and the administrator datasets of that ADOM or of every ADOM. The Global ADOM offers everything.

Relations between datasets#

Datasets point at each other. SATOM describes how — SATOM Builder draws it as a diagram, and you use it to join rows in Jinja:

From To Kind
any appliance_id fleet_appliances.id exact
device (built-in datasets) fleet_appliances.name exact
a sub-object's parent_id its parent type's id exact
a field named like another object type of the same product (a server policy's vserver, server_pool) that type's mkey inferred from the name
server_pool, wpp (built-in) server_pools.name, web_protection_profiles.name exact

🧪Example — Join two datasets in Jinja

{% set pools = {} %}
{% for p in fortiweb_server_pool.rows %}{% set _ = pools.update({p.mkey: p}) %}{% endfor %}

does not work: the sandbox is immutable (no update, no append). Join with a filter instead — and take [0] of a list you checked, because first of an empty list is an error in SATOM's strict sandbox:

{% for pol in fortiweb_server_policy.rows %}
  {% set match = fortiweb_server_pool.rows | selectattr("mkey", "equalto", pol.server_pool) | list %}
  {{ pol.mkey }} → {{ match[0].type if match else "no pool" }}
{% endfor %}

Which dataset should I use?#

You want Use
A quick fleet list or KPIs fleet_appliances, fleet_counts
FortiWeb policies with traffic log, WAF, App ID server_policies_full
Every field FortiWeb keeps for a policy fortiweb_server_policy (or fortiweb_deep_server_policy for the nested tree)
FortiGate firewall policies, addresses, interfaces fortigate_firewall_policy, fortigate_firewall_address, fortigate_system_interface (search fortigate_)
FortiADC virtual servers and pool members fortiadc_load_balance_virtual_server, fortiadc_load_balance_pool__pool_member
Something joined, filtered or totalled Ask an administrator for an admin_… dataset
Your own data (rules, mappings, requests) A data store, read by an app, not a view

The exact keys depend on what your devices hold: search the picker.

Limits#

Limit Value
Rows per built-in dataset 1,000 (audit_recent: 200)
Rows per device-object dataset 1,000
Rows per administrator dataset its query's limit, at most 500
Fields per device-object dataset 120 (plus the 5 fixed columns)
Datasets per view no limit; each is read at every render

In SATOM Builder#

SATOM Builder reads this same catalogue from your SATOM with your token: its Datasets tab and Library list every dataset grouped and searchable; Test data brings their rows (as you would see them) to test on; the Database tab draws their relations and lets you query them with SQL. A dataset an administrator publishes appears there at the next library refresh. → Build with SATOM Builder.
